top.headline: Georgia's Election Board Was Secretly Coordinating With the Group Behind a Flawed 'Dead Voter' Purge Tool
top.blurb: ProPublica found that members and staff of Georgia's State Election Board — including its vice chair and a former member — have been coordinating with Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network, including promoting a flawed voter-roll tool that led a county to challenge ballots from voters later found alive. The board's own chair now says the group has had "undue influence" and must be cut off, as Georgia's governor-elect campaigns to restructure the board entirely.

top.headline: A Maryland Senator Launches a Challenge Against Chuck Schumer for Control of the Democratic Caucus
top.blurb: Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced he'll challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader in the new Congress, where Democrats will hold 55-56 seats after sweeping the midterms. Four senators back him and at least three say they won't back Schumer, whose approval among Democratic voters sits at just 38%, setting up a real test of whether the party wants new leadership.

top.headline: A Top Democrat Wants Republicans to Renew a Warrantless Spy Program Before His Own Party Takes Power
top.blurb: Rep. Jim Himes, the top Democrat on House Intelligence, is urging Republicans to reauthorize FISA Section 702 surveillance during the lame-duck session, before Democrats take control in January — arguing a Democratic-negotiated version would differ, even as civil liberties groups push Congress to wait. The program, which lapsed in June, has reportedly been used to surveil protesters, elected officials and journalists.

top.headline: RFK Jr.'s HHS Quietly Promotes a Project 2025 Alum Who Called the Abortion Pill 'High-Risk'
top.blurb: HHS has promoted Natalie Dodson — a Project 2025 contributor who has criticized the abortion pill mifepristone — into an advisory role under Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., ahead of an FDA safety review due early next year that could tighten access to the drug.

more.headline: A Lame-Duck Defense Bill Could Quietly Fuse the U.S. and Israeli Militaries Together
more.blurb: NDAA provisions being finalized in conference would create a Pentagon post to integrate Israeli weapons firms into U.S. procurement, and ten Democratic senators plus Bernie Sanders are now demanding it be stripped out.

top.headline: Four Nagas Killed in Suspected Militant Ambush on a Manipur Highway
top.blurb: Four Tangkhul Nagas were killed in a suspected ambush near New Haven village on Manipur's Imphal-Ukhrul highway on Friday, a day after a Kuki woman was shot dead in Senapati district. The toll from Naga-Kuki clashes since February has now reached 72.

top.headline: Assam Razes Homes of 132 Bengali Muslim Families Displaced by the 1983 Riots
top.blurb: Authorities in Assam's Lakhimpur district demolished the homes of 132 Bengali Muslim families on Friday — families who say they were singled out since Hindu neighbours nearby were spared. The state has evicted more than 1,900 Muslim families in the past month alone.

top.headline: Shame and Silence: Survivors Detail Decades of Alleged Abuse by an Arrested Mangaluru Priest
top.blurb: Survivors of Mangaluru priest Cyprian Pinto, arrested in October after boys from St Vincent Ferrer Church accused him of abuse, tell The News Minute the alleged abuse spanned decades and multiple parishes. Their accounts, and a witness's, raise hard questions about what the Church knew — and why he kept being handed prominent postings.

top.headline: Families of Jailed Sijimali Mine Protesters Left Without Income as FIRs Pile Up
top.blurb: At least 40 FIRs have been filed against opponents of Vedanta's proposed bauxite mine in Odisha's Sijimali hills since 2023, naming over 150 people, leaving activists like Laxman Naik and Lingaraj Azad jailed with bail denied. Newslaundry traces the toll on the families who lost their sole earners.

top.headline: Delhi's Young Athletes Keep Training Through Toxic Air Because They Can't Afford to Leave
top.blurb: With Delhi's AQI past 400 and GRAP Stage-III in force, young athletes describe training through breathing trouble and persistent coughs; those who can afford it travel to Bengaluru or Odisha, but most families cannot, and university tournaments go on regardless.

top.headline: A Weakened Trump Heads to Asia, Dangling a Three-Way Summit With Xi and Putin
top.blurb: Trump departs next week for the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC in Shenzhen, where he's pushing for a possible three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin — though Beijing is wary and analysts doubt Putin's interest extends past Ukraine. The trip, coming right after Democrats' midterm sweep, tests whether domestic weakness pushes Trump toward calm with Beijing or toward shows of strength abroad.

top.headline: Europe Finally Wins a Seat at Ukraine Peace Talks — But Still Can't Agree Who Should Sit In It
top.blurb: EU leaders meeting in Dublin named the EU bloc plus the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland to represent Europe in the next round of US-brokered Ukraine talks, after fearing they'd be cut out of trilateral negotiations entirely. Leaders remain split on whether Europe needs one single envoy, a rift that undercuts the win even as Germany warns Washington against a "second Anchorage moment."

top.headline: Trump Sidelines His Own Iran Negotiator, Declaring 'We Don't Need a Deal'
top.blurb: Trump posted that the US doesn't need an Iran deal and told JD Vance — the administration's lead negotiator, who favors one — to instead focus on alleged corruption in Democratic cities. The split comes as Iran awaits a US response to its proposed seven-point ceasefire and Hormuz-reopening plan, exposing daylight between Trump, Vance and Secretary of State Rubio on strategy.

top.headline: Can a Caretaker Prime Minister Take Israel Back to War With Iran?
top.blurb: With Netanyahu's government in caretaker status after losing its parliamentary majority, Israeli media report the security cabinet has ordered the military to accelerate Iran-strike preparations, even as Israel's own military reportedly sees no urgent need. Legal experts say a caretaker government likely retains authority for security action, but opposition leaders are warning Netanyahu not to act without oversight.

top.headline: A Debutant's Seven Wickets Can't Break a Stubborn Pakistan in a Rawalpindi Draw
top.blurb: Pakistan's World Test Championship opener against Sri Lanka ended in a draw at Rawalpindi, with the hosts battling to 284/8 on the final day after trailing on first innings. Centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kusal Mendis built Sri Lanka's lead, but Saud Shakeel's 97 and debutant Saqib Khan's seven-wicket haul kept the tourists out of a second innings.

more.headline: South Africa Open a Home WTC Series Against Bangladesh
more.blurb: South Africa, second in the WTC table after beating Australia, host fifth-placed Bangladesh in a two-Test series starting November 15 in Johannesburg.

top.headline: Why Mary Harron's 'American Psycho' Trades Slasher Gore for Wall Street Satire
top.blurb: Scroll's Weekend Watch revisits Mary Harron's 2000 adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's novel, arguing Harron swaps the book's graphic violence for a satirical comedy of manners about Wall Street excess while keeping Patrick Bateman's monstrousness intact. The piece notes the film deliberately leaves open whether Bateman is a real killer or simply fantasizing.

bengal.headline: Calcutta HC Halts Demolition of Jailed Falta Strongman's House
bengal.blurb: The Calcutta High Court stayed, until Monday, the demolition of jailed Falta strongman Jahangir Khan's Srirampur house, questioning whether the state followed proper procedure and gave adequate notice.

bengal.headline: Suvendu Sets a Nov 30 Deadline, Flags a CID Probe Into 57,000 Suspect Housing Beneficiaries
bengal.blurb: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has ordered ineligible Awas Yojana beneficiaries to refund payments by November 30 or face legal action, hinting at a CID probe into 57,000 suspected fake beneficiaries — of roughly 12,000 confirmed wrongful first-instalment recipients, only 1,000 have repaid.

bengal.headline: Bengal Rights Panel Demands a Report on Alleged Custodial Torture, Encounter Threat
bengal.blurb: The West Bengal Human Rights Commission has asked Diamond Harbour police for a report by November 30 on a wife's allegation that her husband was tortured in custody and threatened with a staged encounter.

travel.headline: Fruit Bats Recruited as Unlikely Replanting Partners in Brazil's Atlantic Forest
travel.blurb: Researchers are using synthetic fruit scents to lure seed-dispersing fruit bats — which spread the seeds of over 140 Atlantic Forest plant species — into degraded land to speed up natural reforestation.

happy.headline: A Four-Century Puzzle: Cracking a Shipwrecked Lock From 1583
happy.blurb: A brass combination lock pulled from a Welsh ship wrecked in a 1583 storm once blamed on "an execrable witch" finally clicked open this month, after a metal detectorist's decades-long search and a Cardiff University engineer's micro-CT scan revealed its hidden four-letter code for the first time in over 400 years.

tech_top.headline: OpenAI Lets Its AI Agents Pay With Your Card — Carefully
tech_top.blurb: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, built with Amex, Mastercard and Visa, letting its "dots" agents shop and buy on a user's behalf after each purchase is approved. Agents never see raw card numbers — payment networks issue a single-transaction token instead. It's live only for U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers over 18, and OpenAI isn't taking a transaction cut yet.
tech_top.pm_note: A clean case study in rolling out agentic autonomy with a narrow blast radius — token-scoped permissions and a tight initial user segment instead of a big-bang launch.

tech_top.headline: A Software Update Grounded Every U.S. Flight for Five Hours
tech_top.blurb: A nationwide ground stop hit every departing U.S. flight Friday after sources say an update to the FAA's private communications network triggered a reboot that overloaded routers on an aging air-traffic-control system. The stop lasted about five hours, with over 10,000 delays and 4,000-plus cancellations; officials ruled out a cyberattack.
tech_top.pm_note: A textbook lesson in blast-radius containment — a routine infrastructure update with no rollback plan took down a safety-critical national system, the kind of failure staged rollouts exist to prevent.

tech_more.headline: OpenAI Folds Its Robotics Team Into General Research
tech_more.blurb: OpenAI disbanded its standalone robotics team, arguing its general-purpose models can now control robots directly without a specialized team.

tech_more.headline: A Startup Wants to Put a Bodyguard on Every AI Agent
tech_more.blurb: WhiteMatter raised a $20M Series A led by Blumberg Capital to deploy a dedicated "guardian agent" that polices every AI agent an enterprise runs.

tech_more.headline: A Cambridge Startup Wants to Replace the CPU Entirely
tech_more.blurb: UK startup Tendrils Compute raised $30M, led by Benchmark, to build chips with thousands of parallel cores based on "interaction nets" instead of conventional sequential instructions.

tech_101.text: Letting an AI assistant actually complete purchases for you, not just recommend products. The hard part is doing it safely — e.g. giving the agent a single-use payment token instead of your real card number, so a mistake or a hack can't be reused.

A second AI agent whose only job is watching a first AI agent and enforcing rules on what it's allowed to do. As companies give AI agents more autonomy, this layer is becoming its own product category.

science.headline: Dark Energy May Have Flipped From Negative to Positive 9.5 Billion Years Ago
science.blurb: A team led by Özgür Akarsu at Istanbul Technical University revisited a neglected branch of "teleparallel f(T) gravity" and found a version where dark energy's effective density was negative in the early universe, crossed zero around 9.5 billion years ago, then went positive. The flip falls out of the math rather than being added by hand, and may ease the "Hubble tension" puzzle, though the authors stress the evidence isn't yet strong enough to call it a discovery.

science.headline: Treating a Diamond Defect Like a Molecule Could Speed Up Quantum Computing
science.blurb: A Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory scientist developed a quantum-chemistry shortcut: instead of simulating an entire diamond crystal, he isolates the 16-30 atoms around a defect and treats it as a molecule, letting standard chemistry methods predict how candidate qubits will respond to laser and microwave pulses. The method flagged new boron- and oxygen-based diamond defects as promising qubits, each with a distinct optical signature that could let different qubit types be addressed separately in the same device.

science.headline: Bacteria Have a Hidden Switch That Loosens the Body's Cell Barriers
science.blurb: Researchers led by Dana Graves at Penn found bacteria can loosen the epithelial barriers lining the mouth, gut and lungs — not by destroying the junction proteins, but by triggering a cell protein called FOXO1 to relocate barrier proteins away from the cell membrane within hours. Seen in both cell cultures and mice, the mechanism could inform treatments for heart disease, diabetes and arthritis, all linked to chronic barrier breakdown.

science.headline: A Deadly Virus Jumped From Rodent to Human — Then Spread Person to Person on a Cruise Ship
science.blurb: Two new studies confirm an April 2026 outbreak aboard the cruise ship M/V Hondius — 13 cases, 3 deaths — involved the Andes strain of hantavirus, which spread between people after a single rodent-to-human introduction. Genome sequencing of 10 cases ruled out an engineered or reassorted virus, tying it instead to natural Andes strains from Argentine Patagonia.

science.headline: Earth's Own Atmosphere May Have Supercharged 2024's Monster Solar Storm
science.blurb: Using Japan's Arase satellite, Nagoya University researchers found that 85% of the charged particles driving the powerful May 2024 "Gannon storm" came from Earth's own upper atmosphere, not the solar wind — and the magnetic field dropped far closer to Earth than seen before. The finding suggests atmospheric conditions can amplify a storm's severity, a factor current forecasting models largely ignore.

philosophy.headline: Why Nothing Would Actually Be Complicated
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Andrew T Brenner challenges Leibniz's assumption that "nothing" would be simpler than something. He argues a truly empty world would still contain countless logical, mathematical and moral truths — making it more complex than it looks — so a simple existing reality that explains those truths might actually be the simplest possible world.

philosophy.headline: Equality Is a Practice, Not Just a Belief
philosophy.blurb: Oxford political theorist Teresa M Bejan traces how "equality talk" has accumulated conflicting senses — equal before God or the law was never meant to mean social peers — and how a 17th-century agitator exploited that ambiguity to claim standing with aristocrats. She argues equality survives less as an idea people believe than as a practice sustained by institutions, so it needs rebuilding, not just restating.

philosophy.headline: What Oppressed People Build When They Can't Build Anything Else
philosophy.blurb: Anthropologist Shahram Khosravi describes a "fugitive imagination" — the capacity migrants, refugees and colonized people develop to picture life beyond the borders and categories states impose, from enslaved people's underground literacy to schooling in a refugee camp. States treat this imagination as dangerous because it exposes nationhood itself as a human construction that can be contested.

philosophy_101.term: Why is there something rather than nothing?
philosophy_101.text: Leibniz's classic puzzle: since 'nothing' seems like the simplest possible state, why does a whole universe exist instead? One newer answer says 'nothing' isn't actually simple either — it would still contain abstract truths of logic and math — so the comparison was unfair to begin with.

The ability of people under confinement or oppression to picture and work toward forms of life the ruling system says are impossible. The word 'fugitive' signals that this kind of imagining is itself treated as something to be chased down and suppressed.
